# The C port's tokens (the port text's section 7): one row per Rust compile-fail case of a crate with a C port, naming
# the C form that keeps the case's token, what the C keeps and can't refuse, and the C case that shows it, a t/117
# subtest ("t/117: <name>"), a C test case ("c: <crate>::<module>::tests::<name>"), or a sim or lockstep case
# ("rust: <path>::<name>"), several separated by "; ", or the form outstanding, with "-" for its item, keeps, and check, for
# a case whose C form is still owed. t/117 checks that each case has one row, that each check exists, and that no case
# with a C form of its own is outstanding; the port lands only with no row outstanding.

column5: a ChunksChunkChunk is opaque storage whose layout only chunk.c knows, so no other C names its parts, though the C can't refuse a value of it zero-initialized or with bytes copied into it; outside chunk.c, t/117 refuses a ChunksChunkChunk value or pointer made by an initializer list, a compound literal, a cast of another pointer to its pointer, or a copy or set of its bytes, while a whole-value assignment moves a value already made and an enclosing aggregate's initializer or copy, which zero-fills or copies a member as a whole, isn't seen
column6: t/117: chunk_forged is refused with its diagnostic; t/117: no file but its owner writes a ChunksChunkChunk's opaque storage

column5: a ChunksPackRaw is opaque storage whose layout only pack.c knows, so no other C names its parts, though the C can't refuse a value of it zero-initialized or with bytes copied into it; outside pack.c, t/117 refuses a ChunksPackRaw value or pointer made by an initializer list, a compound literal, a cast of another pointer to its pointer, or a copy or set of its bytes, while a whole-value assignment moves a value already made and an enclosing aggregate's initializer or copy, which zero-fills or copies a member as a whole, isn't seen

column5: a ChunksPacksRootsRootSlot is a capability under clang's analysis: RootSlots' one and fold acquire it inside register's run, and a pin or RootSlot_unused releases it, so a second pin through one slot is refused as a release of a capability not held; msvc's and gcc's builds can't refuse it, a pin that fails releases the slot all the same, and a Pin's drop doesn't give the slot back, so the C refuses a pin after a failed pin or a dropped pin on the same slot, which the Rust's ended borrow allows
column6: t/117: root_slot_registered_twice is refused with its diagnostic

column5: the C has no clone of a ChunksFileTornTail either, which t/117 refuses to find, and outside file.c t/117 refuses a bitwise copy of one into a variable or through a pointer from anything but a call's result, which would leave two storages holding one tail; a copy into a struct's member or an enclosing aggregate's copy isn't seen
column6: t/117: no C clone of a ChunksFileTornTail exists; t/117: no file but its owner copies a ChunksFileTornTail

column5: a ChunksFileTornTail is opaque storage whose layout only file.c knows, so no other C names its parts, though the C can't refuse a value of it zero-initialized or with bytes copied into it; outside file.c, t/117 refuses a ChunksFileTornTail value or pointer made by an initializer list, a compound literal, a cast of another pointer to its pointer, or a copy or set of its bytes, while a whole-value assignment moves a value already made and an enclosing aggregate's initializer or copy, which zero-fills or copies a member as a whole, isn't seen
column6: t/117: torn_tail_forged is refused with its diagnostic; t/117: no file but its owner writes a ChunksFileTornTail's opaque storage

column5: a door that takes a ChunksFileTornTail (cut, append, write_end, of_generation) moves it out of its caller's storage before anything that can fail, so a failed door takes it too, and that storage's next read or door panics as an unwrap of None at the Rust's use of the tail while its drop frees nothing; outside file.c, t/117 refuses a copy of a tail into a variable or through a pointer from anything but a call's result, so no second storage holds the tail a door empties, though it doesn't see a copy into a struct's member or an enclosing aggregate's copy
